# Spartan Logistics Expands Toledo Presence Through Strategic Acquisition

WHITEHOUSE, Ohio, Sept. 9, 2026

WHITEHOUSE, Ohio, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Spartan Logistics, a family-owned third-party logistics provider specializing in warehousing and transportation services, today announces the acquisition of Allen Logistics, a warehousing company supporting customers in Whitehouse, Ohio. The acquisition became effective September 1, 2026.

 

The acquisition adds 100,000 SF of warehousing capacity to Spartan’s existing Toledo operations as the seventh warehouse operation in Northwest Ohio, a market that has been an important part of Spartan’s network and long-term growth strategy. This brings the company to 4.5 million SF of total space and 950,000 SF in Northwest Ohio.

Fura acquires Pacific Northwest freight broker - FreightWaves

## High Rise Logistics acquisition marks deal 7 for AI-powered roll-up 

 Todd Maiden 

· Tuesday, August 11, 2026 

 AI-powered broker Fura has acquired has acquired High Rise Logistics for an undisclosed sum. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Freight broker Fura announced Tuesday that it has acquired High Rise Logistics. The latest transaction marked the seventh acquisition for the Cincinnati-based AI-powered 3PL.

Vancouver, Washington–based High Rise provides flatbed, expedited, truckload and less-than-truckload transportation. It has a large presence in the Pacific Northwest and also offers intermodal, drayage and warehousing services.

Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Fura is rolling up freight brokers and layering tech and automation into their operations to magnify scale.

U.S. 3PL Acquisitions That Are Reshaping American Logistics

# U.S. 3PL Acquisitions That Are Reshaping American Logistics

Discover the most important U.S. 3PL mergers and acquisitions of 2025–2026. Learn which logistics companies acquired which, and why the deals happened.

Aug 5, 2026

The U.S. 3PL industry is in the middle of a consolidation wave. Large logistics providers are acquiring companies to expand into higher-value segments such as healthcare logistics, customs brokerage, fulfillment, managed transportation, and cross-border logistics. At the same time, mid-market and regional 3PLs are buying niche operators to broaden their service offerings, strengthen their geographic reach, and add warehouse capacity. Across the industry, acquisitions have become one of the primary ways logistics companies are growing and differentiating themselves.

Below are some of the most important U.S. 3PL mergers and acquisitions announced or completed between 2025 and 2026, and why each deal matters.

Fort Point Stays Busy with Buy of Yandell

# Fort Point Stays Busy with Buy of Yandell

 

 February 20, 2023| John McNulty

Fort Point Capital has acquired The Yandell Family of Companies, a provider of transportation and logistics services to the wine, food, and beverage industries.

Yandell’s services include transportation, warehousing, and logistics, which are provided by SC Warehouses, an operator of temperature-controlled warehouses; Yandell Truckaway, a provider of transportation and trucking services throughout Northern and Central California; and Yes! Logistics, a provider of freight brokerage services. Yandell was founded in 1945 and is headquartered near San Francisco in Benicia, California.

Source: Yandell Truckaway

RoadOne acquires Higgins Transport Service, expanding southeast logistics presence | Air Freight News

# RoadOne acquires Higgins Transport Service, expanding southeast logistics presence 

Aug 18, 2026

RoadOne IntermodaLogistics announces the acquisition of Higgins Transport Service LLC, a Charleston, South Carolina-based agent of Wall Street Intermodal that provides port drayage and intermodal freight transportation services.

The acquisition expands RoadOne’s drayage and intermodal capacity in the Charleston market, further strengthening the company’s ability to serve importers, exporters, retailers and manufacturers moving freight through one of the Southeast’s most important global trade gateways. In addition to bringing experienced leadership to the market, RoadOne will add 15 drivers to its Charleston operations, strengthening local transportation capacity and complementing the company’s growing warehousing and distribution capabilities across the region.
